units.en: MEFO bills were promissory notes created by Hjalmar Schacht in 1934 to enable the government to fund rearmament, acting through the balance sheet entity ⟦0⟧tallurgische ⟦1⟧rschungsgesellschaft to hide this rearmament from French and British eyes. It also allowed the government to run a great deficit and procure billions of Reichsmarks worth of funds without devaluing the currency. These bills were supposed to mature in six months, after which their recipients would have to be paid and would cause mass inflation, but historically the German government delayed the problem by extending the bills indefinitely. This contributed to part of the reason Germany initiated the war as soon as they did with the ultimate goal of obtaining enough resources for economic self-sufficiency.

This national spirit is designed to represent the state of the German economy, emulating the rapid rearmament in the period of the Four Year Plan and the economic pressure they faced. As such, its main focus is buffing military related construction as well as compelling the player to start the war and solve the economic problem through conquest. Otherwise the player has to abandon it from the start and rebuild the economy from scratch.
Player started the game with ⟦0⟧, as the game progresses the national spirit can evolve into different variants depending on player choices.
There are 3 different variants of the national spirit it can evolve into: ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, and ⟦2⟧
German national focus features 2 different paths for its Economy focus tree: ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧. MEFO Bills will be modified and evolve in accordance to which path the player chooses.

In ⟦0⟧ path, ⟦1⟧ will transform into ⟦2⟧ with heavy penalty. The economy will be ruined from the start, requiring the players to slowly rebuild economy back up stronger than ever, eventually completing ⟦3⟧ and evolve Recovering Economy into ⟦4⟧ before extensive war production begin.

In ⟦0⟧ path, ⟦1⟧ will grow more powerful rather quickly at the cost of looming burdens on the economy that can only be delayed, forcing the players to go to war sooner or later. At the start of the war players will have a choice to transform MEFO Bills into ⟦2⟧ and unlock more measures to buy time. Once enough resources are obtained, players can complete ⟦3⟧ to evolve Economy of Conquest into ⟦4⟧, granting further buff and solving the economic burdens permanently.
In addition, a new national spirit ⟦0⟧ would be added in this path to provide buffs that mainly involves becoming self-sufficient on resource, especially ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧.

Two unique laws, ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧, would also become available. ⟦2⟧ offers a small buff in construction and research with very little resource to market and will be further improved after completing ⟦3⟧, provides stronger buff with no resource to market. ⟦4⟧ can be seen as a stronger version of ⟦5⟧, provides more buff on construction and less penalty on ⟦6⟧ (and can even increase it with ⟦7⟧ Decision).

⟦0⟧ (CGFF) is the main antagonist when dealing with the MEFO Bills system. It represents the cost of channeling every resource into rearmament instead of conventional economic development. CGFF will further increase the Consumer Goods granted by the Economy Law, limiting the number of ⟦1⟧ available for construction and repair.
The following is the formula regarding CGFF:
Total Consumer Goods = Consumer Goods granted by Economy Law ⋅ ( 1 + CGFF ) {\displaystyle {\text{Total Consumer Goods}}={\text{Consumer Goods granted by Economy Law}}\cdot (1+{\text{CGFF}})}
In some cases CGFF can go into the negatives. This will in turn reduce the current consumer goods needed multiplicatively. Thus, there's not need to worry about overdoing it while managing CGFF.
Managing CGFF in "Prioritize Economic Growth" path

If you choose ⟦0⟧ path, apart from losing the benefit of ⟦1⟧, a hefty CGFF penalty would be dumped on you almost immediately. Managing CGFF in this path is pretty straight forward, albeit slow. All you need to do is patiently progress through the focus tree as most of the focuses would reduce CGFF by a bit, in addition to other benefits like new factories. Eventually, after completing ⟦2⟧ the CGFF penalty would be gone completely.

Managing CGFF in "The Four-Year Plan" path

Things get a lot more complicated if you choose ⟦0⟧ path. CGFF started at 10% but would slowly increase every month. If CGFF reached 100%, apart from Consumer Goods, additional penalties would be applied with its severity depending on certain focuses. The only way to stop the growing CGFF permanently is by completing ⟦1⟧, which requires a lot of work. So you must rely on various methods provided in the focus tree to delay the growth and buy time.

After completing ⟦0⟧, not only will CGFF growth be ⟦1⟧ by ⟦2⟧ per month, but you'll also unlock ⟦3⟧ decisions to cut down CGFF numbers directly. Apart from reducing CGFF, some decisions may grant benefits while others may incur penalties. These decisions have the advantage of being available without being in war. However, each of them can only be activated once so they can only buy time for you to prepare for an inevitable war.
The following is the list of ⟦0⟧ decisions:
Consumer Goods Factories factor: ⟦0⟧ Gain Base War support: +2.50%
Consumer Goods Factories factor: ⟦0⟧ Change in popularity in current ruling party: +2.50%
Consumer Goods Factories factor: ⟦0⟧ Gains Collect Scrap Metal for 90 days, which grants: Steel +10
Consumer Goods Factories factor: ⟦0⟧ Gains Import Tariffs for 365 days, which grants: Trade extra resources per factory -1
Consumer Goods Factories factor: ⟦0⟧ Gain Base Stability: -2.50%
⟦0⟧: Has national spirit Gömbös Trade Treaty Is not in Faction with Germany
Consumer Goods Factories factor: ⟦0⟧ Hungary Gets event: Germany Emptied our Accounts Hungary: Gains Germany stole our money: Opinion of Germany -100 Remove Gömbös Trade Treaty

When you're in a state of war, no matter if you declare it or being declared on, the event ⟦0⟧ will show up giving you a choice on whether you want to continue rearmament or not. Choosing ⟦1⟧ will transform ⟦2⟧ into ⟦3⟧, which will inherit most of the benefits including those upgraded via focus. Choosing ⟦4⟧ is ⟦5⟧ unless you plan to choose Prioritize Economic Growth path, as it'll turn ⟦6⟧ into ⟦7⟧, incurring heavy CGFF penalty without any short-term means to lower it and impeding your efforts on completing ⟦8⟧ if you choose Four-Year Plan path.
The Future of the German Rearmament Program
Rearmament has always been our goal

One crucial thing to note is that some national focuses in this tree (namely ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, and ⟦4⟧) will add additional CGFF upon completion. However, if you complete them before the war started then these additional CGFF will be removed upon converting into either ⟦5⟧ or ⟦6⟧. So make sure you complete as many of these focuses as possible before going to war.

⟦0⟧ will also unlocks new decisions to manage CGFF: ⟦1⟧. To seize a country's gold reserve, it first needs to capitulate to you or one of your subject, then you can spend ⟦2⟧ to seize its gold reserve and reduce your CGFF. How much CGFF it can reduce is based on target country's total amount of ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, and ⟦5⟧ in its core territory (not counting its subjects) that's under you or your subject's control (not counting your ally). Only countries in ⟦6⟧ can be seized, and each country's gold reserve can only be seized once.
The following is the formula calculating the effect of ⟦0⟧:

CGFF reduction = (Military factories in target's core + Civilian factories in target's core + Naval dockyards in target's core) 200 {\displaystyle {\text{CGFF reduction}}={\frac {\text{(Military factories in target's core + Civilian factories in target's core + Naval dockyards in target's core)}}{200}}}
After seizing gold reserve, the state modifier ⟦0⟧ will be added to all of the affected states under your occupation for ⟦1⟧ days, which will incur the following penalties:

Completing ⟦0⟧ peacefully will automatically reduce CGFF with ⟦1⟧'s gold reserve. The reduction amount is calculated with the same formula as ⟦2⟧ but no penalties of ⟦3⟧ will be applied. The same goes for completing ⟦4⟧ peacefully and automatically reduce CGFF with ⟦5⟧'s gold reserve.

If you form ⟦0⟧, they will pay you war reparation and your CGFF growth will be ⟦1⟧ by ⟦2⟧ per month as long as they have the ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧. However, this reduction will stop if ⟦5⟧ no longer has ⟦6⟧ or if ⟦7⟧ no longer exists.

The monthly growth of CGFF will ⟦0⟧ with the more non-core territory you conquered. This represents diverting military resource into occupation instead of armament and combat. Despite the description, the increase is not calculated based on the number of states, but based on the amount of ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, and ⟦3⟧ in non-core states directly occupied by you (not counting your subjects). The number is rounded in 0.5% interval and the total monthly growth is capped at 5% per month.
The following is the formula calculating the effect of occupation on CGFF growth:

Total CGFF grwoth = base CGFF grwoth + (Military factories occupied + Civilian factories occupied + Naval dockyards occupied) 50 {\displaystyle {\text{Total CGFF grwoth}}={\text{base CGFF grwoth}}+{\frac {\text{(Military factories occupied + Civilian factories occupied + Naval dockyards occupied)}}{50}}}

Since CGFF growth does not count the factories controlled by your subjects, setting up puppets can help avoiding the penalty in your conquest. You can set up puppets normally through Compliance system, but a more efficient way is completing ⟦0⟧ and setting up puppets through ⟦1⟧ system.

Once you conquered the required capital state the decision to set up the subsequent Reichskommissariat would become available, allowing you to set up puppets immediately without having to wait for Compliance level. Any newly conquered territory which should've belonged to established Reichskommissariats would automatically be transferred to them, minimizing CGFF penalty and micromanagement. Initially only ⟦0⟧ can set up Reichskommissariats, but other continents would become available after completing subsequent national focuses.

Apart from convenience, there are other benefits for utilizing this system. Each Reichskommissariat being set up would strengthen ⟦0⟧ by a bit, which would provide nation wide buff on benefiting through subjects. The Reichskommissariats set up this way would start with a boost of initial Compliance, but they have no core on their territory meaning they're still susceptible to Resistance.
